requirements.requirement: Deploy /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker as a systemd service named 'inventory-worker' on node1
requirements.summary: systemd unit /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service was created with ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker, then enabled and started via systemctl. systemctl is-active/is-enabled show 'active'/'enabled', and systemctl status plus ps confirm the process is running under this unit both before and after a subsequent reboot.

requirements.requirement: Service runs under a dedicated 'inventorysvc' account (not root or a shared account)
requirements.summary: A system account 'inventorysvc' (uid/gid 993, nologin shell, no home) was created with useradd --system --no-create-home. The unit file sets User=inventorysvc, Group=inventorysvc, and ps output shows the running process owned by 'invento+' (truncated inventorysvc) both pre- and post-reboot.

requirements.requirement: Service is correctly configured to run the specified binary (correct ExecStart, no corruption of the source binary)
requirements.summary: The worker script was inspected (POSIX sh sleep loop) and referenced unmodified from /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker in ExecStart. Prepare-time hash/ownership of the binary is unchanged since the executor never wrote to that path.

overall_summary: The core task — running os-comparison-worker as a systemd service 'inventory-worker' under a dedicated 'inventorysvc' system account on node1 — is fully satisfied with direct evidence of account creation, correct unit configuration, and active/enabled/running state confirmed both before and after a full node reboot. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also executed cleanly: healthy pre-restart baseline (boot_id bf8b9d80..., service active), a restart acknowledgement, a confirmed new boot identity (218798de...) cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and full recovery of the service under the correct account post-reboot. The only hygiene concern is a leftover /tmp/reboot.log artifact from the reboot-scheduling command, which is minor and low-risk.
limitations: The public task contract does not explicitly require reboot persistence, so the restart evidence is assessed only as the independent provider-wide protocol, not as a scored material outcome.
No evidence was captured of long-running stability of the service beyond a few seconds after each start/reboot, so behavior over extended uptime is not directly observed.
/tmp/reboot.log was left on disk after the reboot; its exact content was not captured, only its presence in the temporary-files diff.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor actions were narrowly scoped to the task: creating the system account, writing the unit file, and enabling/starting the service, all clearly tied to the material requirements. The subsequent reboot (cmd-826e2d67b80b487c) was performed to satisfy the independent node-restart evidence protocol, not the public task contract, and was bounded (single reboot, immediately re-verified). One minor residue: the reboot was scheduled via 'nohup sh -c ... >/tmp/reboot.log 2>&1', and /tmp/reboot.log persists in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot without being cleaned up afterward — a low-risk logging artifact rather than a security or functional issue. No failed services, no package-health regressions, and no unexpected listening sockets beyond expected chronyd/sshd PID churn from the reboot.
